transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (AE), Ethan (SE), Liam (CSM) - Redwood; Priya (CTO), Daniel (Sr SRE), Selene (Infra), Kieran (Product) - Apollo Finance

Summary (auto): follow-up to last night's production severity where a sudden eviction wave caused throughput collapse and elevated 99th percentile latencies. Goal is to align on immediate mitigations and a plan to reproduce and harden.

[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh we'll keep this short — want to make sure we captured what happened last night and agree owners for the reproducer and pilot. you all good with agenda?
[00:10] Priya: yes, thanks — we got paged at 2am. big customer impact, so we appreciate quick follow-up.
[00:18] Daniel: quick sketch — our telemetry shows a 6x uptick in small parallel requests hitting the same model prefix which caused eviction cascades on the nodes. memory pressure shot up, and KV cache misses spiked.
[00:30] Ethan: yeah that pattern sounds like a hot-prefix avalanche, where the prefix/kv is reloading and then continuous batching is starving. We saw similar in staging but didn't hit production scale.
[00:45] Selene: one thing — our rollout last week changed the sequence length estimator. not sure how that interacts but worth noting.
[00:52] Kieran: customers reported slowness in document parsing flows; they retried and that amplified the burst.
[01:05] Maya: ok quick question about config — are you on the shared hosted plan or dedicated right now?
[01:12] Priya: hosted — we haven't committed to Dedicated; budget cadence next quarter.
[01:18] Maya: got it. that informs mitigations.

[01:30] Daniel: to be blunt, our fallback was pretty noisy. retries plus circuit breakers didn't prevent tail amplification.
[01:40] Ethan: do you have traffic examples we can replay? request IDs or payload samples?
[01:44] Priya: yes we'll share sample IDs. Daniel will dump the logs.

[02:00] Ethan: high-level remediation options: (1) short-term: burst reservation and temporary token-throttling at edge; (2) medium: prefix seeding and cold-cache prewarm; (3) longer-term: Dedicated capacity or pinning model variants with smaller KV working set.
[02:20] Daniel: pref for short-term that doesn't require re-architecting. can you do a burst reservation on hosted?
[02:27] Maya: yes we can provision short-lived burst capacity, depending on region. cost will be elevated but it's fast. I'll get you numbers.
[02:40] Selene: any risk to data residency with that?
[02:44] Maya: no, same region, same controls. but we'll confirm with infra.

[03:00] Kieran: curious about cache seeding — is that the prefix cache thing?
[03:05] Ethan: yes — we can proactively populate KV cache for the hot prefixes you expect, so requests hit cached state and avoid reloads. This requires sample inputs or a replay. Also can shorten retention for cold prefixes while we stabilize.
[03:22] Priya: we can provide examples, but latency sensitive flows are real-time so prewarm window is tricky.

[03:35] Daniel: what's the quickest reproducer you can run? we want a runnable script to show the eviction pattern locally.
[03:40] Ethan: SE plan: create a stream replay that mimics your concurrency and retry behavior, run against a staging cluster with instrumentation (pprof, heap dumps, KV hit/miss counters) and then iterate. should take ~3 business days to get first results.
[03:54] Priya: timeline sounds OK.

[04:05] Maya: security question from procurement — they asked about audit logs and KMS integration. we support SOC 2, and we do KMS for private but for hosted we have customer key support via our KMS integration.
[04:20] Priya: procurement wanted a formal doc with retention windows. can you share the security pack?
[04:25] Liam: yes i'll send the security pack and SOC 2 letter after the call.

[04:40] Selene: also asked about request-level audit traces — we need to map token-level cost to customer tokens for billing.
[04:48] Maya: we can provide token-level traces and per-request latency breakdowns via Console. will include sample dashboards.

[05:05] Kieran: is there any immediate setting we can toggle to reduce eviction risk? maybe lower batch sizes?
[05:12] Ethan: lowering max batch helps latency but increases pressure on GPU utilization and cost. Another knob is KV retention and smaller chunking of cache entries. also prefix-based throttles at the edge for the hot keys.
[05:30] Daniel: ok for tonight we'll try prefix throttling and retry-suppress logic client-side. can you give recommended thresholds?
[05:36] Ethan: yes — based on similar cases, start with a 20rps per-prefix soft limit and exponential backoff with jitter on retry. We'll follow up with exact numbers once we run the reproducer.

[06:00] Priya: one operational ask — can Redwood expose an eviction alert (specific metric) that we can wire to our pager?
[06:07] Maya: yes we have eviction_rate and kv_miss_rate metrics; we'll share alerting rules.
[06:12] Liam: i'll provide a suggested Prometheus alert template.

[06:28] Kieran: any concerns about moving to Dedicated if we wanted to reduce blast radius?
[06:33] Maya: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor and gives predictable throughput. it also allows pinning of models and reserved GPU pools which helps with eviction. Cost is higher but predictable, and you get SLA credits.
[06:48] Priya: timeline-wise how fast could a Dedicated pilot spin up?
[06:52] Maya: if you sign up for a pilot we can provision in 7-10 days depending on region and capacity. For pilots we typically do a 2-week commit.

[07:05] Daniel: curious about resume fallback — last night fallback produced bad outputs when model variant downgraded. is that expected?
[07:12] Ethan: sometimes fallbacks change tokenization nuances or decoding defaults which affects downstream detectors. We can configure function-calling and structured outputs to be consistent across fallbacks, but some behaviors need model-level alignment.
[07:28] Kieran: would quantized variants exacerbate the issue?
[07:32] Ethan: quantization can change output distribution slightly. we recommend running evals on your critical prompt set if you plan to use a quantized fallback.

[07:45] Maya: quick recap and proposed immediate plan: (1) Ethan runs reproducer and shares traces by 2026-02-17; (2) Redwood provides short-term burst pricing and thresholds by 2026-02-12; (3) Customer shares samples and 48h heatmap by 2026-02-13; (4) CSM sets follow-up touchpoint 1 week after pilot start.

[08:10] Priya: sounds good. one more ask — can Redwood share example throttle middleware we can drop into our API gateway?
[08:17] Ethan: yes i'll paste a small node/java example and a config JSON.

[08:30] Daniel: also, can we get a list of exact metrics and log fields to expose — request_id, model_variant, kv_hit, eviction_count?
[08:38] Maya: yes we'll provide a mapping of console fields to telemetry keys.

[09:00] Kieran: procurement also asked about long-term remediation — do you recommend model sharding or more aggressive prefix hashing?
[09:07] Ethan: both are possible: model sharding spreads KV sets across nodes but adds routing complexity. prefix hashing reduces hot-key amplification by distributing prefixes more evenly; that's lower complexity. We can prototype prefix hashing in staging.

[09:28] Selene: do you have any documented runbooks for handling these eviction waves?
[09:33] Liam: we maintain a runbook and will share a trimmed version for customers that includes step-by-step mitigations and alert playbooks.

[09:45] Priya: last question — if we accept a dedicated pilot, how are keys and logs handled?
[09:51] Maya: Dedicated gives you VPC options and KMS integration; logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint or retained with configurable retention.

[10:05] Priya: thanks everyone. let's capture action items.
[10:10] Maya: Ethan, you own reproducer and technical report. Maya for pricing. Liam for security pack and runbook. Priya to provide traffic and request samples.

[10:20] (Crosstalk) Daniel: thanks, appreciate the quick turn.
[10:25] Maya: we'll follow up with a short email summarizing owners and next steps and attach the security pack.
[10:30] Kieran: ok we'll get the samples in the morning.

[10:40] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had occasional speaker swaps and mis-recognized product terms ("Redwood Privet" for Redwood Private, "SOC two" for SOC 2). Some technical terms (pprof, KV) were transcribed correctly intermittently.

References shared during meeting: security pack link (sent via email), sample alert rule template (to be attached), reproducer template (SE to share GitHub gist).
